about: The one door (doc 132, principle `one-door`). A person signs in ONCE, with an account they already have, and that is the only door: a passkey, Microsoft or Google. Every service the estate reaches is declared here, so adding one is ONE ENTRY, never a new login screen and never a stored password. Each entry says what works as a guest (everything should, first), what signing in adds, the narrowest permission it needs (asked for only when the feature is used), and the one place that takes it away. `login` is `primary` when the service is reached through the one door, and `separate` when it has its own credentials: a separate login is the friction register. Each one carries the fix and a date, or a standing reason it cannot go away, and fitness `signin-declared` lets the count only go down. To change the primary identity, change `primary_idp` and the sign-in method on Cloudflare Access: nothing else moves. Never put a secret, a token or a person here.

microsoft.name: Microsoft (Entra ID)
microsoft.why: your Azure app and OneDrive sync already use it, and Cloudflare Access has it built in

google.name: Google
google.why: the other native choice; doc 85 section 2.4 shows Google as the Access sign-in

life-os.name: Life OS and Vantage

asked_when_used.Mail.Read: only when the person taps Read my bank e-mails on Money; read-only, on the device, bank senders only (threat model life-os-bank-mail)

life-os.guest: everything: the whole app works on this device with no sign-in
life-os.signed_in: your data follows you across devices through your own encrypted OneDrive copy; with one more tap, bank alerts in your Outlook inbox fill in spends and cards by themselves
life-os.revoke: Ops, then disconnect, on each device; or remove the app's access in your Microsoft account

command-center-door.name: Command Center door
command-center-door.guest: the hosted door opens and lists your machines with no sign-in
command-center-door.signed_in: the machines it opens ask you to sign in once, through the one door
command-center-door.revoke: nothing to revoke: it keeps no account; clear this device's list

cloudflare-access.name: Your own addresses (Command Center, Chat)
cloudflare-access.guest: none: it guards your own machines, so a sign-in is the point; on the machine itself nothing is asked
cloudflare-access.signed_in: the Command Center and Chat on any device, with no password
cloudflare-access.revoke: ./securax online remove <email>, then remove the person from the primary identity

ai-gateway.name: The AI gateway
ai-gateway.guest: the local model answers with no sign-in, on the machine itself
ai-gateway.signed_in: your own allowance and audit trail, as the signed-in person
ai-gateway.revoke: removing the person from Access ends their allowance; device and API keys are revoked in ./securax

tailscale.name: Private network between your machines
tailscale.guest: none: a private network needs a sign-in; sign in with the SAME account as the primary identity
tailscale.signed_in: your machines and phones reach each other with no open port
tailscale.revoke: remove the device or the user in the Tailscale admin

azure.name: Azure
azure.guest: none: it is a cloud account; ./securax cloud status shows what is signed in
azure.signed_in: the Azure account you already own, with nothing installed
azure.revoke: sign out of the cached sign-in under ~/.securax/cloud; remove the user in Entra

aws.name: AWS
aws.guest: none: it is a cloud account
aws.signed_in: the AWS account you already own, with nothing installed
aws.revoke: sign out of the cached sign-in under ~/.securax/cloud; delete the access key in AWS
aws.fix: AWS IAM Identity Center with the primary identity as its sign-in (it needs AWS Organizations and supports SAML 2.0 and SCIM)

gcp.name: Google Cloud
gcp.guest: none: it is a cloud account
gcp.signed_in: the Google Cloud account you already own, with nothing installed
gcp.revoke: sign out of the cached sign-in under ~/.securax/cloud; remove the member in IAM
gcp.fix: make Google the primary identity, or Workforce Identity Federation with the primary one (it needs a Google Cloud organization)

github.name: GitHub (the code and its releases)
github.guest: the public repository reads with no sign-in
github.signed_in: pull requests, releases and the site build
github.revoke: remove the token or the app's access in GitHub settings
github.standing: A personal GitHub account has its own sign-in and no company single sign-on; the answer is a passkey on it, not a second password.

ai-provider-keys.name: Free AI provider keys (Gemini, Groq, OpenRouter, NVIDIA)
ai-provider-keys.guest: the local model needs no key at all
ai-provider-keys.signed_in: faster hosted answers on the free tiers
ai-provider-keys.revoke: ./securax providers list shows each; delete the key at its provider
ai-provider-keys.standing: Each provider issues its own key at its own sign-up; the estate keeps them in one place (./securax keys) and works with none.
